reviewed_by: Claude Sonnet blind reviewer, batch B8 (g3 na_q2 re-review + na_q3_4-6 + na_q4), 2026-08-12

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Judging a rounded claim like seed 43's '320 ÷ 18 ≈ 15. True or False?' still requires the student to actually estimate the quotient mentally, which is the core skill this competency names.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Dividends run from 2 digits (seed 42's 120) to 3 digits (seed 500's 933) and divisors from 1 digit (seed 605's 2) to 2 digits (seed 500's 63), covering the ranges the competency states.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Rounding to a nearby ten or hundred before dividing (seed 45 flags 100÷22≈80 as false) is a reasonable Grade 3 mental-math move.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All 14 of the 14 samples use the true_false formatter; none of them ever ask the student to pick or type an estimate themselves, only to accept or reject one that's already given.

competency_alignment.rationale: How far the stated estimate sits from the true rounded quotient is what drives difficulty, an axis specific to this competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every dividend and divisor stays within the stated 2-3 digit / 1-2 digit bounds; nothing in the set reaches outside them.
